sections.h2: Where is Westport, Connecticut, and what does the town cover?
sections.html:
Westport is a coastal town in Fairfield County, about 48 miles northeast of New York City, in what is often called the Gold Coast.

Its total area is 33.45 square miles, but only 19.96 of that is land. The rest, 13.49 square miles, is water, so the town includes a long Long Island Sound shoreline. Westport borders Norwalk to the west, Weston to the north, Wilton to the northwest and Fairfield to the east. The 2020 Census counted 27,141 people, and the elevation at the town's listed center is only 26 feet.

The town runs under a Representative Town Meeting, adopted in 1949, with a three-member Board of Selectmen, a Board of Finance and a Planning and Zoning Commission.

Westport has more than ten named areas, from the downtown village to separate shoreline communities.

  • Saugatuck: around the railroad station, with restaurants, shops and offices.
  • Saugatuck Shores: a peninsula that joined Westport in the 1960s.
  • Saugatuck Island: a special taxing district since November 5, 1984.
  • Westport Village: Post Road and Main Street along the Saugatuck River.
  • Greens Farms: the oldest neighborhood, with its own post office and train station.
  • Compo: near the main town beach.
  • Old Hill, Coleytown, Poplar Plains and Staples: older and inland areas.

Saugatuck Island's status as a special taxing district means an owner there may see a separate charge. Ask the tax collector what applies to your address.

sections.h2: What flood rules and weather affect a Westport house?
sections.html:
About 26 percent of Westport residents, and the train station, live within the 100-year floodplain, according to Wikipedia.

The floodplain was breached in 1992 and 1996, damaging private property and flooding the station parking lot. Wikipedia says the town has since put flood mitigation measures in place, including regulations that affect renovations and additions in the floodplain zone. That means a buyer, or you, may face limits on how much can be built or rebuilt on a flood-zone lot.

The climate data lists average yearly precipitation of 48.5 inches and snowfall of 26.2 inches, with a record high of 102 degrees and a record low of minus 15. Ask the town's building and zoning staff about your lot, and check the FEMA map, before you promise a buyer anything.

sections.h2: What is the history of Westport?
sections.html:
Westport was incorporated on May 28, 1835, with land from Fairfield, Weston and Norwalk.

English settlers arrived in 1693 and the area was first called Bankside, then Green's Farm in 1732. Westport was once the leading onion-growing center in the country, until blight collapsed the crop. On April 25, 1777, a British force of 1,850 landed at Compo Beach on the way to destroy supplies in Danbury.

Artists and writers, including F. Scott Fitzgerald, moved here around 1910. From the 1950s through the 1970s, New Yorkers moved out in large numbers. The population rose from 11,667 in 1950 to 27,318 in 1970. The Westport Country Playhouse, founded in 1930, remains a regional theater.

sections.h2: How does Westport's economy and income affect sellers?
sections.html:
Westport has a large finance sector, and its household incomes are among the highest in the country.

sections.h2: What are Westport's schools, roads and train service?
sections.html:
Westport has one public high school, Staples, two middle schools, Bedford and Coleytown, and five elementary schools.

The elementary schools are Coleytown, King's Highway, Greens Farms, Saugatuck and Long Lots. Interstate 95, the Merritt Parkway and US Route 1 all cross the town. Metro-North's New Haven Line has two Westport stops, Westport and Greens Farms. No Amtrak trains stop in Westport, and the nearest Amtrak stations are in Bridgeport and Stamford. The Norwalk Transit District provides bus service.

Sherwood Island State Park covers 234 acres on the Sound, and Compo Beach and Burying Hill Beach are municipal beaches. The town bought uninhabited Cockenoe Island in 1969 for $212,740 so that a utility could not build a nuclear plant there.

sections.h2: Who provides emergency service and what is there to see in Westport?
sections.html:
Westport has a paid, full-time Fire Department, established in 1929, that runs four stations and responds to roughly 4,000 emergency calls a year.

Its equipment list includes six engines, a truck, a rescue unit and a fireboat, and it houses the Fairfield County hazardous materials truck. The police department had 64 sworn officers as of 2020. The fireboat reflects how much of the town is water.

For buyers touring a house, the draw is often the setting. Earthplace is a 62-acre nature center and wildlife sanctuary, Wakeman Town Farm is a working historic farm, the Westport Museum for History and Culture was founded in 1889, and the Museum of Contemporary Art Westport expanded in 2019. These details help you write an honest description of your neighborhood if you list the house yourself.

sections.h2: What taxes and paperwork apply when you sell in Westport?
sections.html:
The seller or the seller's attorney files Connecticut Form OP-236 for the conveyance tax when the deed is recorded with the Westport town clerk.

The state Department of Revenue Services says tax is due on transfers of $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. Westport's town code on the form is 158. Filing can be done through the state's myCTREC system for participating towns, and the form is also available for towns that are not on the system.

  • Ask the tax collector for current balances, including any special district charge.
  • Ask the town about floodplain rules if the lot is near the river or shore.
  • Confirm who pays the escrow or closing items listed in your contract.

We could not open the Westport tax collector or assessor pages for this guide, so we are not giving due dates or the current mill rate. Please ask those offices directly.

sections.h2: What do Westport sellers often face, and what are the options?
sections.html:
Westport sellers can list with an agent, sell privately or accept a cash offer, and the best choice usually turns on the house's condition and the timeline.

  • Older houses that need updating before a financed buyer can close.
  • Flood-zone lots where renovation is restricted.
  • Estates that must clear title before a sale.
  • Owners moving on a short schedule.

A cash offer can remove the lender appraisal step, though you should compare it to what a listing would net after commission and repairs. Send us the address and a short description of the house, and we will explain what a cash purchase could look like in Westport before you decide anything.

faqs.q: What county is Westport, CT in?
faqs.a: Westport is in Fairfield County, in the Western Connecticut Planning Region. The deed is recorded with the Westport town clerk.

faqs.q: What is the population of Westport?
faqs.a: The 2020 Census counted 27,141 residents in Westport.

faqs.q: Is Westport in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Part of it is. Wikipedia reports that about 26 percent of residents and the train station sit in the 100-year floodplain. Check the FEMA map and ask the town about your specific lot.

faqs.q: What is Westport's town code for the conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: It is 158 on Connecticut Form OP-236. The seller or the seller's attorney files the form when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Westport house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell without making repairs, though you should disclose known issues and expect any buyer to price them in. A cash buyer may purchase the house in its present condition.
